column1: # Published reference trajectory hashes for the canonical conformance run
# (NFR-02, NFR-03). Tab-separated. Checked by tools/check_conformance.py.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW OR CHANGING ONE.
# Each row is a published claim: on this architecture, with this compiler
# major, against this C library and with this build type, the canonical step
# steer produces exactly this 64-bit hash. Within one such build, a different
# hash is a determinism bug (NFR-02). Across builds, a different hash is
# expected and is not a failure: cross-platform bit-identity is explicitly NOT
# promised (NFR-03), because libm is not correctly rounded and does not agree
# between platforms.
# The C library is in the key, and it is in the key because it is libm that
# the hash tracks. sin, cos, atan and exp move between glibc versions, and one
# unchanged wheel was measured producing two different hashes on glibc 2.28
# and glibc 2.39. The version is written in full rather than as a major:
# glibc's major has been 2 since 1997, and it is the minor releases that move
# the numbers (ADR-0033).
# Changing an existing hash invalidates every result anybody has ever compared
# against it. It is a release event, it belongs in the release notes, and it
# needs a reason in the commit message: a physics change, an integrator
# change, a change to the conformance scenario, or a change to the state
# layout the hash covers. "The test was failing" is not a reason.
# The L1/rk4 hash is written down twice. The wheel job in .github/workflows/
# ci.yml pins it as a literal, on purpose: it checks an independently built
# wheel against a published number, and reading that number out of this file
# would have the job agree with itself. So a changed L1/rk4 row moves the pin
# in the same commit. tools/check_conformance.py --pin-only checks it did.
# The conformance scenario is defined once, in
# src/orchestration/slipx_sim/include/slipx/sim/manoeuvres.hpp. It uses the
# VehicleParams struct defaults, which are PROVISIONAL and describe no
# measured vehicle (NFR-08). These hashes certify that the arithmetic is
# reproducible. They certify nothing whatsoever about a real car.
# As an observation and not a promise: every x86_64 row below carries the same
# hash for the same case, across GCC 11, GCC 13 and Clang 18. That is evidence
# that the arithmetic does not depend on the compiler here. It is recorded as
# separate rows anyway, because the moment it is collapsed into one row the
# file stops being able to express a compiler that disagrees, and NFR-03 exists
# precisely because one eventually will.
# History. The L2 rows were added on 2026-08-03 when the double-track tier
# landed; they are new claims rather than changed ones, so nothing previously
# published became incomparable by their arrival.
# The six L2 rows were rerecorded on 2026-08-12 when the drivetrain slice
# landed (ADR-0031): the L2 state vector grew from 10 to 13 (steer,
# steer_rate, soc), the ESC and battery bound the drive torque, braking became
# motor braking through the driven axle, and the servo lags the steer command.
# L2 results compared against the previous values are not comparable with
# these. The L0 and L1 rows were re-measured under all three compilers and
# are byte-identical to before, as they must be: no code either tier executes
# changed. The three compiler rows were measured separately, not copied.
# The twelve L1 and L2 rows were rerecorded on 2026-08-12, a second time in
# the same unreleased cycle, when ADR-0032 raised the reference car's
# cornering stiffness by 3.5. The old value put the tyre's force peak at
# 24 degrees of slip angle, which no car reaches, so the reference car could
# not get to its own tyre peak and the MF-lite falling branch was dead code in
# every published figure. The six L0 rows did NOT move and were re-measured
# under all three compilers to confirm it: the kinematic tier has no tyre and
# no cornering stiffness to change. That asymmetry is the evidence the change
# was the one intended.
# Every row below was rerecorded on 2026-08-03 when CORE-07 added the
# per-wheel lagged slip angle to VehicleState. The hash covers the state layout,
# so four extra fields per step moved every row including L0's and L1's, neither
# of which has a tyre transient at all. That is a change to the state layout the
# hash covers, which ADR-0008 lists as a legitimate reason for a hash to move.
# Results compared against the numbers published in 0.1.0a1 are not comparable
# with these. The three compiler rows were measured separately rather than
# copied from one another.
# The eighteen rows were re-keyed on 2026-08-13, not re-measured into new
# values: ADR-0033 put the C library in the key, and every row gained the
# glibc 2.39 it was in fact recorded under, here and on the pinned
# ubuntu-24.04 runners alike. No hash changed and nothing published became
# incomparable. Before this, a run on a different glibc matched a row it was
# never entitled to match and was reported as a determinism bug; it now gets
# the honest "no reference row for this build" instead.
# Columns:
#   system_processor  compiler_id  compiler_major  libc  build_type  tier  integrator  hash
